decision_basis: Neither model cleared the frozen 5/5 seeded-defect plus clean-zero threshold. Both had identical deterministic attribution: three detected, one missed, one ambiguous, and zero clean material findings. KEEP_OPUS_5 preserves the status quo; it is not evidence that the incumbent is adequate. Efficiency cannot decide after a functional block.
limitations: One dispatch per model per case does not establish reliability.
R-CONCURRENCY has no witness and the scorer fails closed when multiple material findings target its override file; both models were ambiguous for that reason.
R-BOUNDARY was missed by both models on this run.
Both models escalated a second counter.sh concern to material only in R-CONCURRENCY, producing the scorer's fail-closed ambiguity; the same concern was a suggestion in other cases.
Temporary experiment agents were primary-mode copies of the Reviewer prompt and permissions because OpenCode 1.18.31 cannot directly invoke subagents.
Opus 5 added prose before JSON in all six responses while Opus 5.5 returned bare JSON in five of six, so the wall-clock comparison includes a prompt-compliance and verbosity difference.
Most of the observed credit reduction follows Opus 5.5's lower catalog rates; aggregate final tokens were only 7.0% lower.
Credits are observed runtime accounting, vary with cache state, and are not reconciled against the GitHub billing interface.
Every dispatch carries a stale historical routing_profile_id from a pre-existing runner constant; resolved configs and concrete experiment agent targets establish model identity.
